output.hypothesis: Product and engineering leads triaging Slack requests will adopt Linear Asks when shown concrete workflow improvements and peer adoption evidence, reducing context-switching and lost requests.

calls.reason: Find past campaign evidence about Linear Asks Slack integration effectiveness and adoption patterns among product/engineering leads
Identify what technical audiences actually engage with on Hacker News regarding Linear and request management
Measure which content types and platforms historically drove adoption for Linear's product features
Check if past claims about Linear Asks adoption benefits were verified or flagged, to avoid unsupported promises
Understand previous campaign goals, editorial scores, and fact/claim patterns for Linear
Identify specific claims about Linear Asks that failed verification to avoid repeating them

decisions.statement: Lead with capability claims (supported, 34 instances) and comparison claims (supported, 2 instances); avoid framing claims (16 editorial) and opinion claims (2 editorial).
decisions.rationale: Claim risk table shows capability claims are supported (34) and comparison claims are supported (2), while framing (16) and opinion (2) claims remain editorial without verification.

decisions.statement: Build messaging around the verified Slack intake workflow: Linear Asks accepts Slack, email, and web forms and converts each request into a Linear issue (fact-48); Slack Asks synchronizes comment threads between Linear and Slack (fact-50); Linear Asks keeps requester conversations connected across Slack, email, and web forms (fact-52).
decisions.rationale: These three facts directly describe the end-to-end Slack-to-issue flow with synced comments that the campaign must demonstrate.

decisions.statement: Anchor credibility with the scale fact: Linear powers over 40,000 product teams (fact-68).
decisions.rationale: A single quantified adoption metric that is already verified and relevant to product teams.

decisions.statement: Address product and engineering leads who triage internal requests from non-technical teammates — specifically engineering teams receiving bug reports (fact-65) and IT/support teams handling hardware, access, and setup requests (fact-66).
decisions.rationale: Audience facts explicitly name these two segments as the ones Linear Asks is designed for.

decisions.statement: Frame the message around turning noisy Slack threads into triage-ready Linear issues without leaving Slack, using the synced comment thread and multi-surface conversation continuity.
decisions.rationale: Fact-48, fact-50, and fact-52 together show the end-to-end Slack-to-issue flow with synced comments and cross-surface conversation continuity.

decisions.statement: Prioritize LinkedIn for long-form posts that link to Linear blog articles that already attracted high Hacker News engagement (e.g., “Planning for Unplanned Work in Linear” 65 pts/33 cmts, “Settings are not a design failure” 488 pts/378 cmts); use X for short clips and screenshots referencing the same articles.
decisions.rationale: Hacker News conversation signals show Linear blog posts repeatedly hit 65–491 points and dozens of comments, indicating the audience consumes long-form content on professional networks and shares snippets on X.

decisions.statement: Do not claim time-bound results (e.g., “cut triage time by 50% in two weeks”) because the only time-bound claims in the risk table are marked time-sensitive and unsupported.
decisions.rationale: Claim risk rows 5 and 6 flag time-bound claims as time-sensitive; no verified time-bound metrics exist in the evidence.

decisions.statement: Open question: No performance rows exist for prior Linear Asks campaigns; measure CTR and conversion on the first two posts before scaling spend.
decisions.rationale: Performance tool returned zero rows, so we have no baseline to set targets.

openQuestions: No performance rows exist for prior Linear Asks campaigns; measure CTR and conversion on the first two posts before scaling spend.
